items.title: Police arrest suspected gunrunner with AK-49 rifles, 228 RPG rounds in Kaduna
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Kaduna State Police Command has arrested a suspected gunrunner and recovered two AK-49 rifles, 228 rounds of RPG ammunition and 275 rounds of 7.62mm AK-47 ammunition in Sabon Gari Local Government Area of the state. The Commissioner of Police, CP Rabiu Muhammad, disclosed this on Thursday during a press briefing in Kaduna, saying the arrest followed a distress call from Yan’Karfe Motor Park in Sabon Gari, Zaria. According to him, the suspect, identified as 39-year-old Kenneth, a native of Delta State, was arrested on August 25 after he was spotted behaving suspiciously while struggling with a sack containing potatoes. He said operatives of the Sabon Gari Division responded swiftly and, upon searching the sack, recovered two AK-49 rifles, 228 rounds of RPG ammunition, 275 rounds of 7.62mm AK-47 ammunition, five AK-47 magazines, and some quantities of suspected hard drugs. “The case is presently under investigation,” the CP said, commending the Divisional Police Officer and his team for their swift response. In a related development, the command said three suspected members of an armed banditry and kidnapping syndicate were arrested along the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway. The suspects, arrested on August 24 following credible intelligence, were identified as Ibrahim Muhammad, 25, alias “Alti”, from Adamawa State; Usman Tukur, 27, alias “Mallam”, from Zamfara State; and Hassan Alhaji Salisu, 23, alias “Tagwaye”, from Doka Village, Gusau Local Government Area of Zamfara State. The suspects allegedly confessed during interrogation to being members of an armed bandit gang operating around Millennium City and other parts of Kaduna State. The CP said the suspects would be charged to court after the investigation concluded. Similarly, police operatives recovered 134 rounds of live AK-47 ammunition during a stop-and-search operation along Kachia Road, Kaduna, on August 25. Muhammad said the ammunition was concealed in a sack carried by a motorcyclist, who allegedly confessed that he had been sent by a notorious armed bandit known as “Yellow Mai-Million” to collect and deliver the consignment. The Commissioner also disclosed the arrest of three suspected armed robbers and rapists following a joint operation by the police, Ahmadu Bello University security personnel and the Civilian Joint Task Force in communities around Rafin Tukurwa, Zaria. The suspects were identified as Jamilu Yau, alias “Jagwa”, 20; Abdullahi Hamisu, alias “Maikudi Santsi”, 25; and Sani Abubakar, alias “Gaye”, 20. According to the CP, the suspects were arrested following complaints and distress calls from residents of Rafin Tukurwa Village, behind ABU Zaria. He said two of the suspects allegedly confessed to the crimes and disclosed that they used a “grave stick” as a charm, allegedly supplied by Abdullahi Hamisu. The suspects were also linked to attacks in Gidan Kira, Magata and Gidan Maranta villages, where victims were allegedly robbed at knifepoint and sexually assaulted. Muhammad appealed to other victims and members of the affected communities to come forward with useful information to assist the ongoing investigation. The command also reported the arrest of a 27-year-old suspected phone thief, Barnabas Amale, who allegedly brandished a pistol after stealing a Tecno mobile phone from a farmer in Idon-Gida, Kajuru Local Government Area. Further investigation reportedly led to the identification of another suspect, Victor Patrick, 37, who allegedly obtained the firearm from a man identified as Oyou Movel, who is currently at large. The police commissioner said detectives also recovered a Toyota Hilux belonging to the Kaduna State Water Board, which was allegedly stolen from Gobarau Road, Ungwan Rimi, Kaduna. He said the vehicle was tracked to Kano State, where the suspected criminal syndicate abandoned it and escaped into the bush following a hot chase by police operatives. In another operation, two suspects, Abdullahi Abubakar and Shehu Sani, both from Makera in Kajuru Local Government Area, were arrested over the alleged armed robbery and vandalization of critical infrastructure at the Infectious Disease Centre, Mando, Kaduna. The suspects allegedly conspired with other members of their gang, who are still at large, scaled the facility’s perimeter fence, tied up five security guards and vandalized the centre’s transformer. The CP described attacks on critical public infrastructure as “serious sabotage” that can threaten public health and safety. He said the command had intensified patrols and raids on suspected criminal hideouts and black spots across the Kaduna metropolis, adding that several dangerous weapons and other exhibits had been recovered. Muhammad also disclosed the recovery of 11 sacks containing dried leaves suspected to be cannabis along the Zaria-Kano Expressway. He said the sacks were abandoned by suspected traffickers who fled after police operatives approached their unregistered Volkswagen Golf Station Wagon while they were loading the items. The Commissioner said the command would continue to intensify intelligence gathering, community engagement and targeted operations against banditry, kidnapping, armed robbery, vehicle theft and other forms of criminality. He appealed to residents to remain vigilant and provide timely information to the police, stressing that community cooperation remained critical to crime prevention. Muhammad commended the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, and Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, for their support to the command. He also appealed to the judiciary to allow the police to continue parading suspects, particularly those arrested in the act or from whom incriminating exhibits had been recovered, arguing that doing so would help sensitise the public and strengthen crime prevention. The Commissioner assured residents that the command would not relent until fleeing suspects were arrested and brought to justice. The post Police arrest suspected gunrunner with AK-49 rifles, 228 RPG rounds in Kaduna appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kayes face aux effets du changement climatique : impacts et solutions
items.description: La region de Kayes est confrontee de plein fouet aux effets du changement climatique. Rarete des pluies, assechement et rarefaction des cours d'eau, secheresse… autant de phenomenes qui bouleversent les conditions de vie des populations et fragilisent les ecosystemes. Face a cette situation, des organisations et des acteurs locaux se mobilisent pour proteger l'environnement et renforcer la capacite des communautes a s'adapter aux effets du dereglement climatique. Mais quelles actions sont reellement menees sur le terrain ? Quelles strategies sont mises en place pour faire face a ces changements ? Et surtout, comment les populations de Kayes s'adaptent-elles a ces nouvelles realites climatiques ? C'est autour de ces questions que nous allons echanger dans cette emission. Pour en parler, nous recevons : M. Demba Traore , charge de communication a la mairie de la Commune urbaine de Kayes. Mme Doumbia Mariam Toure , presidente de l'Association « Musow Seko » ; M. Nigeria : des groupes armés ont extorqué près de cinq millions d'euros de rançons en 12 mois
items.description: Des groupes armes nigerians ont percu environ 4,81 millions d'euros en rancons au cours de l'annee ecoulee, a rapporte l'agence Reuters le 26 août, citant une etude realisee par SBM Intelligence, un cabinet de conseil nigerian specialise dans la securite. Selon l'agence de presse, entre juillet 2025 et juin 2026, plus de 7 800 personnes ont ete enlevees dans le pays, soit une augmentation de 66 % par rapport aux chiffres de l'annee precedente. Reuters a egalement note qu'au moins 1 100 personnes ont ete tuees au cours de cette periode. La majeure partie de ce montant total provenait des rancons percues par une faction du groupe islamiste « Boko Haram ». Selon l'etude, ce groupe arme a percu 90 % des rancons enregistrees pour des enlevements commis dans le nord-est du pays. Cette faction a notamment encaisse environ 4,6 millions d'euros grâce a deux enlevements de masse, au cours desquels plus de 300 personnes ont ete capturees a chaque fois. SBM Intelligence a toutefois ajoute que les montants reels des rancons pourraient etre nettement plus eleves, car les details de nombreux paiements ne sont pas divulgues. L'un des incidents les plus graves a ete l'enlevement survenu dans la nuit du 20 au 21 novembre 2025. a l'epoque, des terroristes ont capture plus de 300 eleves et membres du personnel de l'ecole Sainte-Marie a Papiri, dans l'etat du Niger. Plus tard, l'African Community Network (ACN) a annonce que 50 enfants avaient reussi a s'echapper entre le 21 et le 22 novembre. Pour lutter contre ce genre d'incidents et renforcer la securite, les autorites nigerianes prennent des mesures. Fin juillet dernier, le president nigerian Bola Tinubu a approuve le renforcement de l'armee, qui passera de huit a douze divisions, ainsi que le recrutement de 28 000 soldats supplementaires. Cette decision vise a renforcer la lutte contre les rebelles islamistes, les enlevements et les violences.

items.title: APM crisis: Olopoeyan’s loyalist suspended over alliance dispute
items.description: A fresh crisis has erupted within the Allied Peoples Movement (APM) in Oyo State following the three-month suspension without salary of Kudirat Tijani Olabisi, a Special Assistant to the Executive Chairman of Ibadan North-West Local Government. Olabisi, who is also the APM chairperson in Ibadan North-West Local Government and a known loyalist of the party’s state leader, Alhaji Abdulrasheed Adebisi Olopoeyan, was suspended for alleged anti-party activities, disclosure of official information and other acts of misconduct. The suspension was contained in a letter dated August 19, 2026, signed by the Director of Administration and General Services, Mr Dada Ibukun Oluwaseun, on behalf of the council chairman. The action followed a resolution adopted by the Legislative Council during its plenary on the same day. The council also directed Olabisi to immediately hand over all government property in her possession to the Clerk of the House. However, the suspension has triggered a political controversy, with Olopoeyan alleging that Olabisi was sanctioned because of her refusal to abandon the APM and support a proposed alliance involving political parties in the state. Political sources familiar with the development said Olabisi had declined to participate in the proposed alliance and instead maintained her allegiance to the APM. Reacting to the development, Olopoeyan defended Olabisi, insisting that her loyalty to the party could not amount to misconduct. He said: “She was suspended because she believes in the Allied Peoples Movement. She refused to follow the political parties’ alliance that they wanted her to attend. She remained loyal to the APM and to me as the leader of the party.” Olopoeyan also questioned the legal basis of the proposed political arrangement, arguing that political parties could not simply form an alliance and present it as a recognised electoral platform. “There is nothing like political parties’ alliance in the electoral law of INEC. The Independent National Electoral Commission does not recognise political parties’ alliance,” he said. APM candidates challenge fresh primaries The development comes amid a separate dispute over the APM’s candidates for the forthcoming Oyo State local government elections. Thirty-three chairmanship candidates and 351 councillorship candidates who emerged from the party’s August 3, 2026 primaries have approached the Federal High Court in Ibadan, seeking an order restraining the party from conducting another primary election for the same positions. The plaintiffs are challenging any attempt to organise fresh primaries, arguing that the August 3 exercise was validly conducted and monitored by the Oyo State Independent Electoral Commission (OYSIEC). They said the results of the exercise were subsequently submitted to OYSIEC, arguing that the process should therefore be recognised. The candidates are also asking the court to determine whether OYSIEC has the power to recognise more than one candidate nominated by the APM for the same chairmanship position or ward. The court action has added to the internal disagreements over the party’s leadership and candidate-selection process as the local government elections approach. Olabisi’s suspension has further heightened the controversy, particularly because of her position as the APM chairperson in Ibadan North-West and her reported allegiance to Olopoeyan. The latest development is expected to generate further reactions within the party as the APM grapples with its internal disagreements and attempts to resolve the disputes surrounding its candidates ahead of the council elections. items.title: Femmes, autonomie et finance digitale : Orange Money au cœur d’une révolution silencieuse
items.description: Il suffit parfois d’un simple téléphone portable pour faire tomber des barrières que l’on croyait infranchissables. Dans les marchés, les restaurants de quartier, les kiosques ou les étals de fruits de Ouagadougou, une révolution discrète est à l’œuvre. Elle ne fait pas de bruit, mais elle transforme profondément le quotidien de milliers de femmes. Cette révolution s’appelle l’inclusion financière. Pendant longtemps, gérer son activité signifiait conserver la recette du jour dans un bout de pagne, un portemonnaie vulnérable, courir après la monnaie, traverser la ville pour payer un fournisseur ou encore renoncer à une vente faute de monnaie. Aujourd’hui, un simple paiement Orange Money suffit à sécuriser un revenu, régler un partenaire à distance ou développer une activité sans quitter son commerce. Au-delà de la technologie, c’est une nouvelle forme de liberté économique qui s’installe progressivement. Une révolution silencieuse au cœur des petits commerces. Dans plusieurs localités du Burkina Faso, les femmes utilisent de plus en plus les transactions électroniques pour développer leurs activités. Propriétaires de restaurant, vendeuses de légumes, de fruits, de jus, de gâteaux, etc., elles sont nombreuses à Ouagadougou en particulier à faire d'Orange Money un partenaire sûr pour sécuriser leurs caisses ou éviter les pertes de revenu. Constat ! Pour la responsable du « Restaurant chez Tantie propre », Assita Touré, l’utilisation d’Orange Money dans son entreprise lui procure des avantages énormes. Il est 13h ce vendredi 31 juillet 2026 au « Restaurant chez Tantie propre », situé à quelques encablures du Commissariat central de Ouagadougou. L'heure du déjeuner bat son plein. Les assiettes d’attiéké au poisson, de tô, et de riz gras défilent, les clients aussi. Parmi eux, Alima Ouédraogo, jeune commerçante ambulante, termine son repas. Au moment de payer, aucun billet ne sort de son sac, son téléphone suffit. Quelques secondes plus tard, la transaction Orange Money de paiement est validée. Le geste parait banal. Mais pour Assita Touré propriétaire du restaurant, il symbolise un changement majeur dont elle est actrice à travers sa confiance placée en Orange Money depuis 2024 : « Les pièces sont devenues rares, même le billetage. Ce n’est pas du tout aisé. Imaginez un client qui achète 1000 FCFA et te donne 10 000 FCFA. Non seulement le temps de chercher la monnaie retarde les autres et, pire, la probabilité est forte qu’on n’en trouve pas. C’est pourquoi la possibilité est laissée au client de régler sa facture par Orange Money » , explique-t-elle. Très vite, elle a compris que cette simplicité profite autant à son commerce qu’à ses clients. Elle encourage désormais ceux qui n’ont pas encore de compte à franchir le pas pour la facilité des transactions, la simplicité des paiements instantanés rapides et sécurisés. « Quand ils arrivent et m’expliquent qu’ils n’ont pas de compte de monnaie électronique ou préfèrent la liquidité, je les rassure qu’avec les transactions électroniques, surtout Orange Money, les soucis se conjuguent au passé. Beaucoup de mes clients sont venus me remercier après l’ouverture du compte », se réjouit-elle. Pour elle, Orange Money n’est plus seulement un moyen de paiement, c’est un outil qui facilite la vie. Avec Orange Money, la caisse devient un compte sécurisé. Quelques kilomètres plus loin, devant le siège de Faso Mêbo, Segdi Lompo, vendeuse de gâteaux, ne laisse plus les clients passer par absence de monnaie. Elle dispose d’un compte commercial Orange Money pour attirer les clients qui préfèrent gagner du temps en circulation. Il est 16h10 mn, lorsque nous sommes arrivés, dame Lompo s’est mise debout pour classer soigneusement ses biens en tas de cinq (05). Les prix proposés sont de 100F et 250 F. Visiblement, la carte commerciale Orange Money est attachée. Toute souriante, elle explique qu’avec le compte Orange Money, elle arrive à contrôler les entrées et sorties de sa caisse. « Avant, je perdais des clients à cause des monnaies liquides. Maintenant ma caisse est mon compte Orange Money. Je ne cours plus pour chercher de la monnaie, je contrôle mieux mes recettes et mes clients sont satisfaits. », argue-t-elle. Vendeuse de gâteaux, Segdi Lompo se réjouit de choisir Orange Money pour fructifier ses activités. Cette phrase résume à elle seule l’une des principales transformations apportées par la finance digitale. La recette du jour n’est plus exposée aux risques de vols ou de perte, elle est sécurisée. Pour des milliers de commerçantes, cette évolution représente bien d’avantage qu’un simple confort. Elle constitue un véritable levier d’autonomie financière qui change des vies. Pour Nelly Kondé épouse Sombié, Secrétaire Générale de Orange Money Burkina Faso, l’inclusion financière dépasse largement la question du paiement numérique. « Gérer un revenu, ce n’est pas seulement le recevoir. C’est pouvoir le conserver en sécurité, le déplacer instantanément, le faire fructifier et décider librement de son utilisation. C’est cette autonomie financière, souvent discrète mais profondément transformatrice que nous mettons entre les mains des femmes burkinabè » , soutient-elle. Elle identifie trois bénéfices majeurs : Le premier est la sécurité : les commerçantes ne sont plus contraintes de transporter leur recette avec des risques de vol ou de perte. Le deuxième est la traçabilité : chaque transaction laisse une trace et permet un meilleur suivi des recettes et des dépenses. Le troisième est l’ouverture : une commerçante installée à Koudougou peut désormais régler son fournisseur à Ouagadougou sans quitter son étal. La secrétaire générale Orange Money Burkina Faso, Nelly KONDE SOMBIE : « un compte Orange Money, alimenté et mouvementé régulièrement, dessine un historique qui devient une identité financière pour des femmes, qui, hier encore, n’existait pour aucune institution financière. » Autre fait majeur, la SG Orange Money Burkina Faso s’est dit convaincue d’une chose : « aucune femme burkinabè, où qu’elle se trouve, quel que soit son niveau d’instruction ou son activité, ne doit se sentir exclue de la révolution du paiement numérique. Cela suppose pour elle d’étendre le réseau de distribution de Orange Money jusqu’aux villages les plus reculés, de concevoir des produits à l’écoute réelle des usages féminins, et de faire de l’éducation financière un effort permanent plutôt qu’une campagne ponctuelle » . Une porte d’entrée vers d’autres services financiers Pour Nelly SOMBIE, le compte Orange Money représente une porte d’entrée vers d’autres services financiers auxquels une branche de la population n’avait pas accès : « L'ambition la plus profonde de la monnaie électronique : est d’être un premier pas vers un écosystème financier complet. Un compte Orange Money, alimenté et mouvementé régulièrement, dessine un historique qui devient une identité financière pour des femmes qui, hier encore, n'existaient pour aucune institution bancaire. » Cette identité ouvre progressivement la voie vers l'épargne formalisée, vers des produits de microcrédit adaptés aux cycles d'activité féminins souvent courts ou saisonniers, et demain vers des solutions d'assurance accessibles, pensées pour protéger une activité informelle contre les aléas. Pour elle, « C’est précisément là que se situe l’ambition la plus profonde de Orange Money Burkina Faso. Nous avançons sur ce chemin en construisant des partenariats avec des institutions financières et des acteurs de la microfinance, convaincus qu'aucun acteur ne peut, seul, construire l'inclusion complète : elle se bâtit à plusieurs mains » . La promesse de l’interopérabilité L'interopérabilité, c'est la promesse que l'argent d'une femme ne reste plus prisonnier d'un seul canal. Aujourd'hui, une utilisatrice peut se heurter à des frontières invisibles entre son compte mobile et le compte bancaire de son fournisseur, entre son opérateur et celui de sa cliente dans une autre région, voire dans un pays voisin. Chaque pont bâti entre ces systèmes notamment avec les banques, ainsi que les autres acteurs de la microfinance est une frontière de moins pour une femme entrepreneure dont l'activité, elle, ne connaît pas ces cloisonnements. C'est un enjeu que la BCEAO a compris, et que Orange Money Burkina Faso porte avec conviction, notamment à travers les chantiers régionaux de la plateforme interopérable des systèmes de paiement dans la Zone UEMOA portée par la Banque Centrale des États de l’Afrique de l’Ouest, parce qu'une économie qui veut inclure pleinement ses femmes ne peut se permettre de la fragmenter en systèmes qui ne se parlent pas entre eux. Innover pour renforcer la confiance des femmes Cette inclusion passe également par la confiance qui constitue le premier capital d’un service financier. Orange Money Burkina Faso renforce continuellement ses dispositifs de sécurité afin de mieux protéger les utilisatrices contre les tentatives d’arnaques. Des messages de sensibilisation diffusés en langues nationales, des dispositifs de détection des opérations suspectes, la simplification des procédures de signalement ou encore l’impossibilité d’utiliser sa date de naissance comme code confidentiel : autant de mesures qui visent à sécuriser davantage les usages. Des initiatives qui répondent à des situations bien réelles. Assita TOURE, propriétaire du restaurant « Tantie propre » reconnaît avoir été victime d’un client mal intentionné qui lui avait affirmé avoir effectué un paiement sans qu’il soit réellement crédité sur son compte à elle. Depuis, elle vérifie systématiquement chaque transaction. Une vigilance qui complète les mécanismes de protection mis en place par Orange Money Burkina Faso. Quand l’analphabétisme cesse d’être une barrière L’une des plus grandes victoires de cette transformation est sans doute celle-ci : elle ne laisse personne en marge. A la sortie de l’Agence d’Information du Burkina Faso, Aminata OUEDRAOGO vend des fruits. Depuis le début de l’année 2025, elle utilise un compte commercial Orange Money. Aminata Ouédraogo, vendeuse de fruits : «malgré que je ne sois pas instruite, j’utilise un compte commercial Orange Money pour satisfaire mes clients » En cette soirée du 31 juillet, aux environs de 17 h, les usagers s’activent pour regagner leurs domiciles. Certains s’arrêtent pour s’approvisionner en oranges avec dame Ouédraogo. Par souci de monnaie, Salif Kientega, un usager de la route, fait recours à la transaction électronique via un compte commercial Orange Money de la commerçante. « Je suis pressé car la pluie menace. Je préfère les paiements instantanés que de fatiguer la dame à courir chercher la monnaie qu’elle n’est pas sûre d’obtenir. J’ai un compte Orange Money et avec le sien, le pari est gagné. C'est simple, fiable et rapide » , confie-t-il. Dame OUEDRAOGO, touche du doigt la réalité de l’inclusion financière avec Orange Money « bien que je ne sois pas instruite, j’utilise un compte commercial Orange Money pour satisfaire mes clients ». Cette phrase résume à elle seule l’ambition portée par Orange Money Burkina Faso. Parce que l’inclusion financière ne peut être réservée aux seules personnes instruite. Dans de nombreux cas, les femmes analphabètes brisent les barrières et s’intéressent de plus en plus aux paiements instantanés. Pour améliorer leurs connaissances financières et numériques et leur permettre d’utiliser ces services en toute sécurité, Orange Money Burkina Faso a pris le taureau par les cornes. Pour la Secrétaire Générale, l’éducation financière constitue le socle d’une inclusion durable. Elle souligne que les services Orange Money sont pensés pour répondre aux besoins de tous les profils d’utilisateurs et pour toutes les composantes de la société Burkinabé, avec une priorité accordée à la simplicité d’accès, à la facilité d’utilisation et à la sécurité des transactions. Selon la vendeuse du jus, Mariam Ilboudo, le revenu de son entreprise est gardé dans le compte Orange Money. A la Zone d’Activités Commerciales et Administratives, Mariam ILBOUDO vend des jus. Sur sa glacière, un QR Code Orange Money permet aux clients de régler instantanément leurs achats. « Depuis que j’utilise Orange Money, je n'ai jamais eu de souci lié aux transactions. Je ne peux que remercier la société pour la confiance placée en ses clients et les différentes mesures prises pour s’assurer de la fiabilité et de la sécurité des transactions » , s’exclame-t-elle. Dans le même ordre d’idée, elle trouve que si les paiements instantanés n’existaient pas, il fallait absolument en créer. C’est pourquoi elle invite les autres femmes qui hésitent à s’y lancer et à prendre attache avec les responsables d'Orange Money Burkina Faso. Son témoignage rejoint celui d’Assita, de Segdi, d’Aminata et de milliers d’autres femmes. À l’aide du code QR Orange Money affiché sur la glacière, il suffit de scanner pour faire la transaction. Toutes racontent finalement, la même histoire, celle d’une activité devenue plus simple, d’un revenu mieux protégé, d’un commerce plus dynamique, d’une femme qui gagne chaque jour un peu plus en autonomie. Au Burkina Faso, l’inclusion financière n’est plus seulement une ambition. Elle se vit au quotidien, sur les marchés, dans les restaurants, les kiosques, les commerces de proximité et jusque dans les villages les plus reculés. Acteur majeur de la finance digitale et unique Etablissement de Monnaie Electronique agréé par la Banque Centrale des Etats de l’Afrique de l’Ouest au Burkina Faso, Orange Money Burkina Faso poursuit cette ambition : faire en sorte qu’aucune femme ne soit exclue de la révolution des services financiers numériques. Car derrière chaque femme qui accède aux services financiers se dessine une famille plus résiliente, une économie plus forte et un Burkina Faso plus inclusif. Et cette transformation ne fait que commencer. Oumarou RABO (Correspondance particulière) Faso7 L’article Femmes, autonomie et finance digitale : Orange Money au cœur d’une révolution silencieuse est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Affaire des leaders syndicaux de la BCRG : la partie civile réclame 100 millions GNF de dommages et intérêts
items.description: Les réquisitions et plaidoiries dans l’affaire opposant le ministère public à trois leaders syndicaux de la Banque centrale de la République de Guinée (BCRG) se sont déroulées ce jeudi 27 août 2026 devant le tribunal correctionnel de Kaloum. Le verdict est attendu ce vendredi 28 août. Les prévenus sont Aboubacar Sidiki Camara, secrétaire général adjoint du syndicat de la BCRG, Aboubacar Yansané, chargé de la santé, de la sécurité et de l’hygiène au travail, et Momo Camara, chargé des affaires sociales du syndicat. Ils comparaissent libres. Ils sont poursuivis pour des faits présumés d’« outrage à agent, violences et voies de fait », à la suite d’une plainte de l’adjudant-chef Daouda Sankhon, aide de camp du gouverneur de la BCRG, Karamo Kaba. Les faits se seraient produits le 6 août dernier dans les locaux de la BCRG, dans le contexte des revendications du syndicat concernant notamment la prime scolaire destinée au personnel pour contribuer à la scolarisation de leurs enfants. À l’audience de ce jeudi, la partie civile a réclamé la condamnation des trois prévenus au paiement de 100 millions de francs guinéens à titre de dommages et intérêts. De son côté, le parquet a requis que les prévenus soient déclarés coupables des faits qui leur sont reprochés et retenus dans les liens de la prévention. Pour la répression, il a demandé qu’ils soient condamnés chacun au paiement d’une amende d’un million de francs guinéens. La défense, estimant que ses clients n’ont commis aucune infraction, a plaidé leur relaxe pure et simple. Les avocats des prévenus ont également sollicité la condamnation de la partie civile, Daouda Sankhon, pour procédure abusive, au paiement de 100 millions de francs guinéens au profit des trois leaders syndicaux. Après les différentes observations des parties, le tribunal correctionnel de Kaloum a mis l’affaire en délibéré et a renvoyé le prononcé de sa décision à ce vendredi 28 août 2026. Elisa CAMARA L’article Affaire des leaders syndicaux de la BCRG : la partie civile réclame 100 millions GNF de dommages et intérêts est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: La viande devient de plus en plus rare et chère sur les marchés du Mali
items.description: a Bamako comme dans certaines capitales regionales, l'acces a la viande devient de plus en plus difficile. La hausse du prix du betail et les difficultes d'approvisionnement pesent sur les bouchers et les consommateurs. Les acteurs de la filiere proposent des solutions pour ameliorer l'approvisionnement des marches. Dans la capitale malienne (Bamako), a Bafoulabe ou encore a Koulikoro , trouver de la viande a un prix abordable devient de plus en plus difficile. Chez certains bouchers, les etals sont moins fournis, tandis que le prix du betail reste eleve. Selon des vendeurs, le coût eleve du betail reduit fortement leurs marges et peut meme entraîner des pertes apres l'abattage. « a chaque fois qu'on achete et qu'on egorge un bœuf, c'est une perte. Hier encore, mon oncle a achete un bœuf a 620 000 FCFA et, apres l'abattage, il a enregistre une perte de 45 000 FCFA », temoigne un acteur de la filiere. Un autre vendeur decrit une situation similaire : « Les bœufs sont devenus tres chers et difficiles a trouver. Acheter un bœuf a 500 000 F pour obtenir a peine 100 kg de viande rend la vente deficitaire. On ne sait plus comment faire face a la hausse du prix du betail. » La filiere appelle a ameliorer l'approvisionnement Le president de l'interprofession de la filiere betail-viande, Mamoudou Diallo reconnaît les difficultes actuelles d'approvisionnement. Il estime qu'une amelioration de l'offre pourrait contribuer a faire baisser les prix de la viande. Selon lui, le retour des animaux transhumants pourrait notamment renforcer l'approvisionnement des marches. « Pour que le prix baisse, il faut attendre un peu le retour des animaux transhumants », explique Mamoudou Diallo. Mais il preconise egalement la creation et l'ouverture de points de vente de betail a proximite des grandes agglomerations. Des points de vente peripheriques Pour les acteurs de la filiere, la multiplication de parcs et de points de vente securises en peripherie des grandes villes permettrait de faciliter l'acces au betail et de reduire le recours a certains intermediaires. Ainsi selon eux, cette organisation pourrait faciliter l'approvisionnement de Bamako et des capitales regionales. Des dispositions qui vont contribuer a une baisse des prix. Le poisson et le poulet gagnent du terrain dans les menages En attendant une eventuelle baisse des prix , certains menages adaptent leurs habitudes alimentaires. Le poulet de chair et le poisson de mer prennent davantage de place dans les marmites, selon les consommateurs. L’article La viande devient de plus en plus rare et chère sur les marchés du Mali est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: Nepal flood death toll climbs to 359 as around 1,000 remain missing
items.description: Devastating floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have killed at least 359 people, Nepali police said in an update on Thursday, a day after the disaster. “As of 5pm [on] Thursday, 359 people have died,” Nepal Police said in a statement. Chinese state media had earlier reported “major casualties” from a mudslide at a Tibet border hub with three dead, taking the total killed to at least 362. A terrifying clip of surveillance video from the Chinese side of the frontier shows a massive wall of mud and debris crashing over a building several stories high on Wednesday morning, engulfing it as dozens of people ran for their lives below. The surge swept away buses and cars like they were toys. Many of the missing are foreign tourists, officials said of the disaster, which the US Geological Survey believes was caused by a glacial collapse that sent a flow of debris engulfing areas along the way. The tsunami-like rumble of water and mud struck villages and towns on the path of two rivers — Bhote Koshi and Trishuli. When Nepal’s death toll stood at 273, 823 people, including 579 Nepali and foreign tourists, remained out of contact, according to the country’s disaster agency. These included nearly 100 Chinese nationals, according to Beijing’s foreign ministry. The Chinese embassy was “seeking further verification” from Nepali authorities, ministry spokesman Lin Jian told reporters. Later, about 100 missing Indian visitors and 25 Chinese workers were located by rescuers in Nepal, authorities said. Across the border, Chinese state media said 558 people, including 260 foreigners, were still missing. Meanwhile, the US State Department said 90 Americans were missing after the Nepal floods. “We’re currently tracking 90 Americans who may be impacted by the flood, currently unaccounted for,” a spokesperson said. The State Department said it could confirm that three Americans had been rescued and it was not aware of any US deaths. Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah left by road for Bidur in one of the worst-affected districts of Nuwakot to assess the flood situation, his office said on social media. Raju Bhadel, 56, a businessman in Nuwakot, recounted receiving a call from his brother-in-law in distress. “They were crying and said their entire house had been swept away. Three family members were rescued, but his brother is still missing,” he said. Also at Nuwakot, teacher Manok Mishra witnessed “nine trucks being swept away by the floods, including people”. This frame grab taken from video released by the Armed Police Force of Nepal on August 26, 2026 shows rescue workers carrying a person after massive floods and landslides in Rasuwa. —AFP ‘Inland tsunami’ Rescuers waded through mud and sludge to look for survivors after floodwaters buried the lower floors of multi-storey buildings. Among those hunting for their missing family members was Subash Khatani, who told AFP he was looking for his big brother. “He is among the missing from Rasuwa. That’s why we are out to search for him,” he said. Among the missing tourists from more than two dozen countries, 177 were from India, 63 were from the United States, 34 from Australia, 33 from Britain and 25 from Canada. Others included tourists from Malaysia, the Netherlands, Portugal, South Africa and South Korea, Nepal’s tourism board said. Hiking company Himalayan Glacier told AFP that 47 people from a group, including two children, were missing in Nepal. “Our teams are checking hospitals where victims are coming in,” said the company’s director Sanket Pandey. The sudden rush of mud and debris was “like an inland tsunami, travelling nearly 170 kilometres down the Bhote Koshi valley into Central Nepal”, said environmental historian Ruth Gamble of La Trobe University. “It is a popular route for international tourists travelling from Kathmandu to Lhasa,” she added. “It was a huge gush of mud coming straight towards us,” said Keshav Prasad Baral, a 68-year-old survivor being treated in a Nepali hospital. “As it got closer, it kept rising higher and higher. When I saw it enter our home, I tried to grab my wife’s hand and take her to the terrace. But she was swept away by the mud.” A helicopter ferried him to safety four hours later. “My wife is still somewhere beneath the mud,” he added. “She’s gone.” Another survivor said he saved himself by clinging to a mango tree as he watched the house where he had been working disappear. Rasuwa, in the north of Nepal, was the first district to be affected. But deaths have been reported from seven Nepali districts in total as the floodwaters raged through to Chitwan in the south, on the border with India. “There is devastation everywhere we look,” said Tula Bahadur BK, a health worker in Rasuwa. “The settlements next to the river have been completely swept away. Five of my own relatives are missing.” The Nepali Army was carrying out flights and had rescued scores of people, while others living near the river in danger zones had been told to relocate. China’s leader Xi Jinping said that “the most urgent task is doing everything possible to search for and rescue the missing people”, according to CCTV . Tibet government officials mobilised nearly 800 emergency workers and 150 vehicles as well as sniffer dogs and speed boats to help the rescue efforts, China’s state-run news agency Xinhua said. The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) said it was dispatching emergency supplies including blankets, first aid kits, stretchers and body bags. “Entire villages and market areas have been wiped out,” said David Fisher, the Nepal head of IFRC. The US State Department said it was sending a disaster response adviser and providing assistance of $500,000. Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said details on the disaster were scant. “Nepal … is a developing country,” he said. “It doesn’t have the resources that an event like that would have in Australia, so information is difficult.” UN teams and partners were sending supplies and personnel to support affected Nepali communities, Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said. Glacial collapse The cause of the disaster was not immediately clear in the hours after it occurred early on Wednesday, but the US Geological Survey said it was a glacial collapse that caused seismic activity and the “catastrophic” downstream impacts in Nepal and Tibet. “This event was initially reported as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake,” it said. “Additional analysis of nearby seismic stations, long-period seismic waves, and satellite imagery led to the determination that the seismic event was instead a glacial collapse and debris flow, and that no earthquake had occurred.” Climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of glacial lake floods and glacial collapses. Residents look at a street submerged by mud following flash floods and a landslide disaster in Devighat, in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 26, 2026. —AFP Qianggong Zhang, head of climate and environmental risks at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), warned of the potential for a second flood. “With a blockage still lodged upstream on the Nepal-China border river, authorities warn a second flood may occur,” he told AFP. Many trekking companies were not running tours during the monsoon season, but there remain significant numbers of travellers, including pilgrims, in the region. Experts cautioned that a lingering blockage in a river could produce an additional flood. Among sites hit by the flood was Syabrubesi, the gateway to the popular trekking areas, as well as by pilgrims travelling to the base of Mount Kailash, a holy site for Buddhists and Hindus. Traffic authorities in Tibet’s Shigatse said roads in the area were “at risk of mudslides and unsafe for passage”. Buddhist spiritual leader the Dalai Lama said that he was praying for all those killed in devastating floods in Nepal and Tibet. “I pray for all those who have lost their lives, and offer my sympathy and heartfelt condolences to the bereaved and to all those affected by this tragedy,” he said in a statement.

items.title: 2027: DLA candidate Adebisi vows to defeat Tinubu
items.description: The presidential candidate of the Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA), Moses Adebisi, has declared that he will defeat President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election and emerge as Nigeria’s youngest elected president. Adebisi made the declaration on Thursday during an interview on Arise TV, where he explained his decision to enter the presidential race and outlined his party’s strategy for challenging the established political parties. The DLA was registered by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in February 2026 after 171 political associations initially applied for registration. INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, had said 14 of the associations met the initial pre-qualification requirements, but only the DLA satisfied all the legal conditions following the final assessment. Explaining his decision to contest the presidency, Adebisi said he was motivated by the desire to contribute directly to solving Nigeria’s challenges after spending time abroad. He expressed confidence in his ability to defeat the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) and its presidential candidate, Tinubu, in 2027. “As I, Moses, am usually called, I am the only person that has the capacity to defeat the Bola Ahmed Tinubu-led APC government come 2027 in Nigeria. You can actually take my word for that,” he said. Adebisi said the DLA had deliberately maintained a low profile while building its political structures, describing the approach as its “submarine strategy”. “They never saw us coming. Nobody saw us coming at all, but we came anyway,” he said. According to him, the party plans to combine the strategy with grassroots mobilisation and an “underdog approach” to challenge the dominant political parties during the election. Adebisi also described the DLA as the only political party registered by INEC between 2022 and 2026, noting that it emerged from a competitive process involving numerous political associations. He said his candidacy represented a generational shift in Nigeria’s presidential politics, stressing that he was the youngest candidate in the 2027 presidential race. “The presidential candidate of the DLA is the youngest presidential candidate or the incoming president of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, the youngest,” he said. Why I returned from US Adebisi said his decision to return to Nigeria and enter politics was influenced by calls from Nigerians urging him to participate directly in addressing the country’s problems. Before joining partisan politics, he said he was involved in community-based empowerment programmes, including initiatives supporting low-income market women and digital literacy projects for secondary school students. He said his organisation provided computers and volunteers to communities across parts of the South-West, North-Central and the Federal Capital Territory to assist students preparing for computer-based examinations. Adebisi said his interest in political leadership also led him to study economic transformation models in other countries, particularly China’s economic reforms launched in 1978. He disclosed that he travelled to China, including Beijing and Shanghai, to study the country’s economic transformation and the policies he believed contributed to its emergence as a major global economic power. “I was like, what are the things that make people emerge politically? What are the things that make people win elections and how do people succeed?” he said. He added that his study of China’s economic reforms, alongside aspects of the American liberty agenda, formed part of his preparation for political leadership. “That is why I’m here, that I’m the right man for the job. And I’m the one that will defeat Tinubu this 2027,” Adebisi said. The 2027 presidential contest is expected to feature President Tinubu seeking another term alongside candidates from opposition and emerging political parties, with parties expected to intensify grassroots mobilisation as the election approaches. items.title: Immersion patriotique obligatoire au Djôrô : Clap de fin sous une note de satisfecit
items.description: Le gouverneur de la région du Djôrô, Siaka Barro, a présidé, le jeudi 27 août 2026 à Gaoua, la cérémonie de clôture de l'immersion patriotique obligatoire des bacheliers, marquant ainsi la fin de la formation de la deuxième promotion dans la région. À l’issue de l’immersion patriotique, les appelés ont promis de transmettre les valeurs acquises à leur entourage. Lancée le 27 juillet 2026, l'immersion patriotique obligatoire des bacheliers de 2026 de la région du Djôrô s'est achevée le jeudi 27 août 2026 à la place de la Nation de Gaoua. Au terme des 30 jours d’immersion, 2 211 appelés constituant la deuxième promotion de l'immersion patriotique obligatoire dans la région du Djôrô ont achevé la formation. Pendant un mois, les appelés ont suivi une formation destinée à renforcer leur sentiment d'appartenance nationale, leur esprit de discipline et leur engagement citoyen. Également, ils ont été outillés sur le civisme, le patriotisme, la cohésion sociale, le vivre-ensemble, le secourisme… Prenant la parole au nom de ses camarades lors de la cérémonie de clôture de l'immersion patriotique obligatoire, Wend-Raabo Syntiche Koadima a exprimé leur reconnaissance au Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, pour cette initiative. Selon elle, cette immersion a permis aux participants de renforcer leur discipline, leur esprit de solidarité et leur sentiment d’appartenance à la nation. « Malgré les difficultés liées à l’éloignement des familles et aux changements d’habitudes, les appelés ont appris à partager, à s’entraider et à privilégier l’intérêt général », a-t-elle souligné. Au terme de cette immersion, Wend-Raabo Syntiche Koama a invité ses camarades à faire vivre ces valeurs au-delà de l'immersion et à devenir des citoyens responsables, engagés et déterminés à contribuer à la construction d'un Burkina Faso meilleur, souverain et prospère. Avant de saluer l'engagement des encadreurs, des personnels militaires, paramilitaires et civils, ainsi que de tous ceux qui ont contribué au bon déroulement de la formation. Le commandant du 22e Régiment d’infanterie commando (RIC) de Gaoua, le chef d’escadron Farabé Gaston Kienou, a, pour sa part, salué le déroulement de la formation. Il a rappelé que l’encadrement avait pour principales missions d’assurer la discipline, la formation et l’accompagnement des appelés durant les 30 jours d’immersion. « Nous avons été investis d’une mission dont les composantes ont été l’encadrement, la discipline et la formation. Je pense qu’on a réussi la mission parce que tout s’est bien passé », a-t-il déclaré. Pour le commandant du 22e RIC de Gaoua, Gaston Fabéré Kienou, le Burkina Faso a gagné des fils dignes encore pour les générations à venir. Le chef d’escadron Farabé Gaston Kienou a également relevé une évolution positive dans le comportement des jeunes au cours de leur séjour. « Vous avez vu le changement qui a eu lieu. Je pense qu’on a réussi à changer les esprits de ces appelés à l’immersion, à mettre la graine du patriotisme en eux », a-t-il souligné. A l’en croire, le Burkina Faso a gagné des fils dignes encore pour les générations à venir. C’est pourquoi, il s’est dit convaincu que les effets de cette immersion se feront sentir dans les comportements des jeunes au cours des prochaines années. « Mettre en pratique les acquis » Au terme des 30 jours d'immersion patriotique obligatoire, le gouverneur de la région du Djôrô, Siaka Barro, s'est dit satisfait de la formation reçue par les appelés. « Nous avons vu des jeunes qui sont formés sur tous les plans, que ce soit sur le plan militaire ou civil », a déclaré le gouverneur, citant les enseignements relatifs au patriotisme, à la cohésion sociale, au vivre-ensemble, à la construction de l'État, aux techniques d'intervention opérationnelle rapprochée et aux réflexes à adopter en cas d'attaque. Pour Siaka Barro, les démonstrations pratiques présentées lors de la cérémonie de clôture témoignent de l'assimilation des enseignements reçus durant la formation. Le gouverneur a surtout invité les appelés à mettre en pratique les connaissances acquises et à les transmettre à leur entourage. « C'est de les appeler à mettre en œuvre ces formations qu'ils ont reçues et aussi à former ceux qui sont autour d'eux », a-t-il insisté. Le gouverneur Siaka Barro a invité les appelés à transmettre à leur entourage les valeurs de patriotisme et de cohésion sociale acquises durant l’immersion. Selon lui, cette dynamique doit contribuer à l'émergence d'une nouvelle génération de Burkinabè disciplinés, ordonnés, engagés et prêts à défendre la nation. Il a estimé que les acquis de cette immersion produiront leurs effets dans les années à venir. « Nous avons une génération montante qui fera la fierté du Burkina Faso de façon générale », a-t-il soutenu, appelant les jeunes à œuvrer à la construction d'un Burkina Faso nouveau, souverain et respecté. La cérémonie s'est achevée par des démonstrations pratiques, notamment en ordre serré, en techniques de combat et en secourisme, suivies d'un défilé final marquant la fin du mois d'immersion patriotique obligatoire. items.title: Tinubu swears in Enitan as Head of Civil Service
items.description: President Bola Tinubu on Thursday swore in Abel Enitan as the new Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, HOCSF, following the retirement of his predecessor, Didi Walson-Jack. Enitan took the oath of office at a brief ceremony held at the State House, Abuja, formally assuming the top administrative position in the Federal Civil Service. His assumption of office followed the retirement of Walson-Jack, who stepped down after attaining the statutory retirement age of 60. The formal transfer of responsibility also took place on Thursday, with Walson-Jack and Enitan signing the relevant official documents before the outgoing Head of Service handed over the official transition note to her successor. Presenting the document, Walson-Jack said it covered the period from August 14, 2024, to August 27, 2026. The handover was subsequently sealed with a handshake between the outgoing and incoming Heads of Service. Enitan, an indigene of Osun State, became the most senior Permanent Secretary in the Federal Civil Service before his appointment as Head of Service. He had served as a Permanent Secretary for seven years and seven months, during which he held senior positions in several government establishments. His previous postings included the Ministry of Police Affairs, Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and the Office of the Vice President, before his deployment as Permanent Secretary in the Federal Ministry of Education. Tinubu had on August 19, 2026, approved Enitan’s appointment as the new Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, with the appointment taking effect on August 27. In announcing the appointment, the President said Enitan brought “considerable institutional experience and a deep understanding of how the Federal Civil Service works” to the position. Tinubu charged the new Head of Service to consolidate ongoing reforms and innovations in the civil service while deepening professionalism, efficiency and accountability across the system. The President also tasked Enitan with ensuring that the Federal Civil Service remained professional, merit-driven, innovative and responsive to the needs and aspirations of Nigerians. According to Tinubu, the new Head of Service must build on existing reforms to strengthen the capacity of the service to deliver effective and efficient public administration. The President commended Walson-Jack for her service to the nation, particularly the reforms and innovations recorded in the Civil Service during her tenure. Walson-Jack assumed office as Head of the Civil Service of the Federation in August 2024 and retired after completing her statutory service. Who is Abel Enitan? Enitan was born on December 12, 1966, and began his education at Ajibode Grammar School, Ibadan, before proceeding to the College of Arts and Science, Ile-Ife. He obtained a Bachelor of Science degree in Finance and Banking from the University of Lagos in 1988 before joining the Federal Civil Service. His extensive experience across several ministries and government institutions culminated in his emergence as the most senior Permanent Secretary prior to his appointment as Head of Service. With his assumption of office, Enitan becomes responsible for providing administrative leadership to the Federal Civil Service and driving the implementation of government reforms aimed at improving efficiency, professionalism and service delivery. The post Tinubu swears in Enitan as Head of Civil Service appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bangladesh to 'positively' consider joining Makkah pact if invited: foreign minister
items.description: Bangladesh would consider joining the Makkah Pact “positively” if invited by founding members, Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman told parliament on Thursday. “Joining the pact or not has not come yet, as it is subjected to the intention of the parties involved in the pact. If they invite Bangladesh to join, then we will definitely consider it positively,” the foreign minister said, assuring parliament that Dhaka would assess the potential benefits before making any decision to join. “More importantly, we have to keep in mind that it [the Makkah Pact] is the Muslim world’s self-defence mechanism,” he added. “And this is our family’s, the Muslim family’s, internal matter. So, there is nothing for others to be concerned about.” Separately, opposition leader and Bangladesh Jamaat-i-Islami Ameer (chief) Shafiqur Rahman said on Thursday that joining the Makkah Pact was Bangladesh’s “own decision.” “If Bangladesh takes a decision in the interests and needs of the country and nation, no one else needs to worry about it,” he said in a statement on Facebook. Earlier this week, Bangladesh’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir said Dhaka had expressed interest in joining the pact. “If there is one [agreement] in West Asia, if there is a security agreement between Islamic countries, then it is not unusual to go there. Let’s see. The matter is being viewed positively,” said Kabir. ​​​​​​​Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed the joint defence agreement at a trilateral summit in Makkah on August 7, pledging to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif during the summit at Al-Safa Palace. The tripartite pact empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them, and reflects their “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”. Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both. In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”. The pact has been welcomed by the United States, Bahrain and Somalia, with Turkiye expecting Egypt to join the pact “in the next stage”.

items.title: Gourma/Faso Mêbo : Des agents de SUNU Assurances contribuent à la confection des pavés
items.description: BURKINA-GOURMA-CONTRIBUTION-FASO-MEBO-SUNU Gourma/Faso Mêbo : Des agents de SUNU Assurances contribuent à la confection des pavés Fada N’Gourma, 27 août 2026 (AIB)-Des agents de SUNU Assurances de Fada N’Gourma, conduite par leur responsable Moumouni Zerbo, ont participé ce jeudi 27 août 2026 sur le site de l’Agence Faso Mêbo, à la confection de pavés, en réponse à l’appel patriotique du Président du Faso, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Les agents de SUNU Assurances ont participé ce jeudi 27 août 2026, sur le chantier de l’Agence Faso Mêbo de Fada N’Gourma, à la confection de pavés destinés aux travaux d’aménagement pour la construction du Burkina Faso. « Aujourd’hui, nous avons jugé bon de venir mettre notre main dans la pâte aussi pour accompagner l’initiative que notre camarade président Ibrahim Traoré nous a lancée, en rappelant que chacun doit construire son pays », a déclaré le responsable de SUNU Assurances Fada, Moumouni Zerbo. Pour lui, la construction du Burkina Faso ne saurait être l’affaire des seules autorités. « Ce n’est pas à lui seul de faire le travail. Nous tous, on a quelque chose en tout cas à faire pour construire le pays », a soutenu camarade Zerbo. Il a invité les citoyens qui n’ont pas encore rejoint la dynamique à emboîter le pas, estimant que la contribution à l’initiative Faso Mêbo peut prendre plusieurs formes. « Pour ceux qui n’ont pas encore mis leur main dans la pâte, nous les invitons également à faire le pas. Le pas, ce n’est pas forcément de façon matérielle. Vous pouvez contribuer aussi à votre manière en soulevant quelques briques ou en déposant un peu de mortier, et c’est génial », a-t-il exhorté. Selon le responsable de SUNU Assurances Fada, chaque contribution, aussi modeste soit-elle, participe à alléger la tâche des travailleurs mobilisés quotidiennement sur le chantier. « Cela pourra en tout cas faciliter la tâche avec les éléments qui travaillent chaque jour ici. Je vous invite tous à participer à l’initiative Faso Mèbo », a conclu Moumouni Zerbo. La participation des agents de SUNU Assurances à la confection des pavés illustre ainsi l’engagement d’acteurs du secteur privé aux côtés des populations pour accompagner les initiatives de construction et de développement du Burkina Faso. items.title: SYPALA 2026: ‘Anti-corruption without enforcement is meaningless’ — Senanu
items.description: The African Union’s elaborate anti-corruption and governance framework will have little impact unless member states move beyond adopting laws and institutions to enforcing them and imposing visible consequences for violations, the Chairperson of the African Union Advisory Board Against Corruption (AUABC), Edem Senanu, has cautioned. He said Africa had made significant progress in establishing continental rules and institutions to promote accountability, transparency and good governance, but a persistent gap between commitments and implementation continued to undermine public trust. Mr Senanu made the observation in a presentation on “The Accountability Deficit: Corruption, Transparency and Public Trust” at the 2026 Students and Young Professionals African Liberty Academy (SYPALA) at the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), on Wednesday, August 26. The four-day programme, convened by the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education in partnership with UPSA, brought together young people from across Africa to engage in discussions on governance, economic freedom, development and public policy. Beyond laws Mr Senanu’s presentation examined whether the African Union (AU) was delivering on its governance and anti-corruption commitments and challenged participants to assess the continent’s performance not by the number of treaties signed or institutions created but by tangible results. He noted that the AU had developed a broad governance architecture comprising instruments such as the African Union Convention on Preventing and Combating Corruption, the African Charter on Democracy, Elections and Governance and Agenda 2063. Institutions such as the AUABC and the African Peer Review Mechanism (APRM) also provide platforms for monitoring, peer learning and promoting accountability. However, he said the effectiveness of those mechanisms depended heavily on the willingness and capacity of member states to translate continental commitments into action. The presentation assessed the AU as relatively strong in rule-making, moderate in institution-building and monitoring, but weak in enforcement and consequences, with its impact on public trust remaining insufficient. Mr Senanu said the central challenge was the implementation gap, pointing out that the existence of laws and anti-corruption institutions did not automatically guarantee independence, adequate resources or effective enforcement. “Ratification, legislation and institutional creation do not establish independence, resources or enforcement,” the presentation noted. According to him, the accountability deficit has consequences that extend beyond public administration and financial management. It affects the distribution of public resources, the quality and cost of public services, the competitiveness of businesses and citizens’ confidence in state institutions. The presentation noted that scarce resources could be diverted, the cost of public services increased and poorer communities were disproportionately affected when accountability systems were weak. It further cited data from Afrobarometer showing that across 39 surveyed African countries, fewer than half of respondents trusted presidents, the police or the courts, while only 37 per cent expressed trust in Parliament. Mr Senanu therefore argued that transparency should not end with the publication of government reports. For information to translate into accountability, he said, citizens must be able to understand what has happened, which recommendations remain outstanding and whether those responsible for wrongdoing have faced appropriate consequences. From paper to performance He proposed that the AU should measure its governance performance through a chain covering five areas: commitment, institutional capacity, actual practice, consequences and public value. That approach, he said, would help prevent what he described as “paper compliance”, where countries receive credit for adopting laws without demonstrating that those laws are being enforced. Among the reforms proposed were the establishment of a public AU accountability dashboard to track country commitments and implementation, strengthening the independence and capacity of the AUABC, making follow-up central to peer reviews and linking governance commitments to national budgets. He also called for stronger protection for whistle-blowers, journalists, auditors, courts and civil society organisations, alongside greater use of open contracting, beneficial ownership registers, asset-declaration systems and cross-border asset recovery mechanisms. Young Africans challenged The intervention at SYPALA placed the responsibility for Africa’s governance future squarely before its emerging generation of leaders, professionals and policy thinkers. Mr Senanu’s assessment concluded that the AU had built a substantial accountability architecture, but implementation remained uneven and its impact on citizens was still insufficient. The presentation consequently challenged young Africans to shift the continental conversation from whether Africa has enough governance frameworks to whether those frameworks are actually changing citizens’ everyday experiences. The next phase of African integration, it argued, must transform shared continental values into shared verification and, ultimately, visible consequences.

items.title: ICT, afternoon court sittings can help clear case backlog – Supreme Court nominee
items.description: Supreme Court nominee Anthony Forson Jnr has proposed greater use of information and communication technology (ICT) and afternoon court sittings to help the judiciary reduce its backlog of cases. Appearing before Parliament’s Appointments Committee on Thursday, August 27, Mr Forson said technology and more flexible working arrangements could significantly improve the efficiency of the courts. He said his experience at the Ghana Bar Association, where he helped digitise its operations, had shown him the potential of technology to improve the administration of justice. “My record at the Ghana Bar Association speaks for itself, where I digitised all the operations of the Ghana Bar, and it’s something that I will strongly support the CJ on,” he said. Mr Forson expressed confidence that, with the necessary resources and commitment, the judiciary could deploy ICT to accelerate the disposal of cases. “Of course, if there are funds, I am 100% sure the know-how to help with the disposal of the backlog of cases using ICT. It is doable,” he said. He argued that technology should therefore be central to efforts by the Chief Justice to tackle delays in the judicial process. Mr Forson also acknowledged that some reforms could face resistance from stakeholders, particularly lawyers who may have to adjust to new working arrangements. He cited afternoon court sittings as an example. “For example, I believe that there should be afternoon court sittings. There will be opposition because the lawyers will say that they need their rest, but we have to move forward,” he said. While he believes additional sitting hours could help reduce the workload on the courts, Mr Forson maintained that ICT offers the strongest solution to the backlog. “But I believe that the strongest point to use is ICT, and it is doable,” he added. His proposals come amid concerns over delays in the disposal of cases and the growing workload of Ghana’s courts, with increasing calls for reforms to improve efficiency and access to justice.

items.title: High feed cost, poor financing threaten fish production — FG
items.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has identified high feed costs, inadequate access to quality fish seed and broodstock, poor financing and weak fish-health systems as major challenges limiting fish production in Nigeria. Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Dr Adegboyega Oyetola, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja while inaugurating the Technical Committee on Accelerating Fish Production in Nigeria. Oyetola said the challenges had contributed to a significant gap between domestic fish production and national demand, with implications for food security, household incomes and foreign exchange. He also identified post-harvest losses, inadequate cold-chain and storage infrastructure, gaps in research and innovation, weak data systems, inadequate standards and traceability, and poor market development as constraints to the sector. According to him, “Domestic production remains substantially below national demand, with consequences for food security, household incomes and foreign-exchange resources.” The minister said the high cost of production, particularly fish feed, was undermining farmers’ ability to expand output, while limited access to quality seed and broodstock was restricting productivity. He added that weak fish-health and biosecurity systems, coupled with inadequate cold-chain facilities, continued to expose the sector to production risks and post-harvest losses. Oyetola further listed limited access to affordable finance as a major constraint, saying research and innovation gaps, poor data, and inadequate market systems must also be addressed to unlock the sector’s potential. He said the transfer of fisheries and aquaculture functions to the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy had provided a stronger institutional platform to tackle the challenges as part of Nigeria’s broader blue economy development. The minister said the government remained committed to increasing sustainable domestic fish production, strengthening the fisheries value chain and progressively reducing the country’s dependence on fish imports. Oyetola said the newly inaugurated committee would review recommendations from a strategic roundtable on accelerating fish production held by the ministry in collaboration with the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies, NIPSS, on October 29, 2025. He charged the committee to move beyond policy formulation and develop a practical roadmap for addressing the sector’s challenges. “Your assignment is not to develop another policy or establish a parallel programme,” the minister told the members. He directed the committee to assess the roundtable recommendations against existing policies, laws, government programmes and institutional mandates, determining which should be adopted, refined, integrated into existing frameworks or subjected to further study. The committee is also expected to map existing government, private-sector and development-partner initiatives to prevent duplication and ensure efficient use of resources. Oyetola said the final report must contain an implementation matrix detailing priority interventions, responsible institutions, timelines, indicative costs, funding options, performance indicators and required approvals. The report is also expected to identify opportunities for private-sector investment, public-private partnerships and development finance. The committee, chaired by the Permanent Secretary of the ministry, Mrs Fatima Sugra Mahmood, has eight weeks to submit its report. Unos rastrean las riberas en busca de supervivientes; otros avanzan con maquinaria pesada entre el lodo, los escombros y las carreteras destruidas. Durante el día, los helicópteros han sobrevolado las localidades que permanecen aisladas y han llevado suministros a sus habitantes. La deuxième édition de l’Immersion patriotique obligatoire (IPO) s’est tenue du 27 juillet au 26 août 2026 sur l’ensemble du territoire nationale. Pour le compte des régions du Goulmou, de la Sirba et de la Tapoa, les appelés de l’IPO ont effectué leur sortie officielle, jeudi 27 août 2026, après un mois de formation civique et patriotique à Bogandé, à Fada N’Gourma, à Kantchari et à Diapaga. Sous la pluie, devant parents et autorités, cette deuxième cuvée, forte de 2246 immergés, a entonné, fièrement, le Ditanyè et l’hymne de la promotion. En ces instants solennels et uniques dans leur vie, les jeunes bacheliers ont offert un aperçu de leur quotidien sur les différents sites de l’immersion, à travers un sketch sur le civisme et le vivre ensemble, un slam sur le patriotisme, des démonstrations sur les techniques d’intervention opérationnelle rapprochée et la grande parade. Au-delà, le quotidien des appelés était rythmé par des enseignements sur la discipline, la sociologie et l’histoire du Burkina Faso, la géopolitique, les enjeux sous-régionaux et internationaux, la vision souverainiste du Burkina Faso et le développement endogène, entre autres. « Nous ne trahirons jamais la mère patrie » Au nom de ses camarades, Abdoul Abas Kafando a exprimé sa gratitude au Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, pour son engagement en faveur de la formation, de la responsabilisation et de l'éveil de la jeunesse. « Mon capitaine, merci de croire en nous », a-t-il dit. Il a salué, également, les encadreurs, les formateurs et l’ensemble des Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS) qui, durant leur séjour, ont fait preuve de patience, de rigueur et d’engagement. Selon lui, ce sacrifice leur a permis de devenir aujourd’hui des citoyens nouveaux. En retour, les immergés, par la voix du jeune Kafando, se sont engagés à défendre la cause de la Révolution quoi que cela leur coûte. « Dès cet instant, nous devenons les ambassadeurs de la révolution, du patriotisme partout où le devoir nous appellera, dans nos universités, dans nos futures fonctions et au sein de nos communautés. Nous sommes la jeunesse consciente. Nous ne trahirons jamais la mère patrie », a-t-il déclaré. Le gouverneur Ram Joseph Kafando a remercié toutes les personnes physiques et morales qui, d’une manière ou d’une autre, ont contribué à la réussite de l’IPO. Beyond the GH¢500bn Target: The silent workforce blind spots in Ghana’s AI strategy (Part I)
items.description: The Silent Workforce Blindspots in Ghana’s AI Strategy: PART I The ambition driving Ghana’s digital policy landscape is clear. The Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations recently unveiled the Republic of Ghana National Artificial Intelligence Strategy (2025–2035), projecting a target to inject GHc500 billion into our national economy over the next decade. Across corporate boardrooms in Accra, Kumasi, and Takoradi, executives celebrate artificial intelligence as an efficiency booster. Yet behind this wave of enthusiasm lies a profound macroeconomic paradox. What is individually rational for a single firm cutting overhead can prove collectively disastrous for an economy driven by consumer spending. As corporate Ghana aggressively replaces human workers with automated software, we risk walking blindly into an “AI Layoff Trap”—a structural cycle where short-term corporate efficiency erodes the broader consumer demand required to sustain national economic growth. The Anatomy of the White-Collar Trap The mechanics of AI displacement differ sharply from past industrial revolutions. Previous technological shifts automated manual labor while expanding white-collar management. Today’s generative workflows invert that dynamic, directly targeting routine cognitive tasks: basic legal research, entry-level bookkeeping, front-end software debugging, and customer service operations. In Ghana, these very roles form the vital intake pipeline for thousands of tertiary graduates entering the job market each year. When companies eliminate entry-level administrative, banking, and IT support positions in the name of productivity, they create top-heavy ‘Diamond-Shaped Organizations’—firms with senior leaders at the apex, but with their foundational base cut away. By eliminating junior roles, companies sever the organic learning loops and informal mentorship through which university graduates evolve into experienced domain leaders. Furthermore, displacing white-collar professionals systematically contracts domestic purchasing power, directly threatening the bottom lines of the consumer-facing businesses that automated those roles in the first place. Exposing the Policy Blindspots While the National AI Strategy rightly emphasizes infrastructure expansion and computing power, it leaves three critical structural blindspots unaddressed: 1. The PAYE Revenue Collapse: State revenue planners treat AI as a pure engine of GDP growth. However, GDP calculations do not automatically translate into state tax receipts. In Ghana, Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) income taxes collected from formal white-collar workers represent a predictable source of public revenue. Every junior accountant or bank officer replaced by an offshore AI model represents a permanent reduction in the domestic income tax base. 2. Invisible Foreign Exchange Capital Flight: Relying entirely on foreign-owned AI foundation models extracts wealth from our economy. When Ghanaian enterprises integrate external platforms, every API call and monthly user license requires recurring payments in US Dollars, accelerating capital flight and pressuring the Cedi. 3. The Coding Illusion: Policy initiatives like the ‘One Million Coders Programme’ assume that teaching basic software programming guarantees future-proof employment. Yet basic front-end coding is precisely what generative AI models automate most efficiently. Meanwhile, non-automatable, physical, and high-touch technical fields remain underfunded. Coming up, in Part 2, we explore the four-point legislative blueprint required from Parliament to fix these gaps and protect Ghanaian workers. The writer, Mawuli Dzodzome Agbenorto, is a Public Servant & IT Consultant. He can be reached via: mdmawuli@gmail.com
